== Euclidean geometry ==

In Euclidean geometry, the triangle inequality states that the sum of the lengths of two sides of a triangle is always larger than the third side.

For instance, in $\triangle ABC$

[[File:Triangle.png|250px|center]]

$$
a+b>c \\
a+c>b \\
b+c>a
$$

== Generalisation to vector spaces ==

Let $V$ be an [[inner product space]] over $\mathbb{F}$.

$$\forall u,v\in V,\; \left\| u+v \right\| \le \left\| u \right\| + \left\| v \right\|.$$

{{Hidden proof}}
$$
\begin{aligned}
\left\| u+v \right\|^2
&=\langle u+v,u+v\rangle
=\langle u,u\rangle+\langle v,v\rangle+\langle u,v\rangle+\langle v,u\rangle\\
&=\langle u,u\rangle+\langle v,v\rangle+\langle u,v\rangle+\overline{\langle u,v\rangle}
=\left\| u \right\|^2+\left\| v \right\|^2+2\operatorname{Re}\langle u,v\rangle,\\
\text{Note }\operatorname{Re}\langle u,v\rangle
&\le|\langle u,v\rangle|
\stackrel{\text{Cauchy-Schwarz}}{\le}\left\| u \right\|\left\| v \right\|,\\
\left\| u \right\|^2+\left\| v \right\|^2+2\operatorname{Re}\langle u,v\rangle
&\le\left\| u \right\|^2+\left\| v \right\|^2+2\left\| u \right\|\left\| v \right\|
=(\left\| u \right\|+\left\| v \right\|)^2,\\
\Rightarrow \left\| u+v \right\|^2 \leq (\left\| u \right\|+\left\| v \right\|)^2,\\
\because \left\| . \right\| \geq 0 \\
\therefore \left\| u+v \right\|&\le\left\| u \right\|+\left\| v \right\|
\end{aligned}
$$
{{End hidden}}
